statement: Let Q satisfy the hypotheses of Theorem 1, and fix either Dirichlet (B = D) or Neumann (B = N) boundary conditions. Let (uj)j≥1 be any complete orthonormal eigenbasis of L2(Q) for the corresponding Laplacian, with −∆Buj = λ2 j uj, 0 ≤ λ1 ≤ λ2 ≤ · · · , where frequencies are listed with multiplicity. A set S ⊂ N has density one if #(S ∩{1, . . . , N})/N → 1. Then the following conclusions hold. 1. There is a density-one set Sint such that, for every classical order-zero pseudodifferential operator A whose Schwartz kernel is compactly supported in Q × Q, lim j→∞ j∈Sint ⟨Auj, uj⟩L2(Q) = ∫︂ Q×S1 σ0(A) dµ. Here the Euclidean metric identifies unit covectors with Q × S1, and σ0(A) is restricted to them. 2. Let Γ be the regular boundary, the union of the three open sides. For λj > 0, let hj = λ−1 j and define the Cauchy data on the open sides by ub j = {︄ hj ∂νuj|Γ, B = D, uj|Γ, B = N, where ν is the outward unit normal. Write B∗Γ = {(s, η) ∈ T∗Γ : |η| < 1}, using arc length s and signed tangential covector η on each side. There is a density-one set S∂ ⊂ {j : λj > 0} such that, for every a ∈ C∞ c (T∗Γ) and a properly supported order-zero semiclassical quantization Ah = Oph(a), lim j→∞ j∈S∂ ⟨Ahj ub j, ub j⟩L2(Γ) = 2 π Area(Q) ∫︂ B∗Γ a(s, η)wB(η) ds dη, where wD(η) = √︂ 1 − η2, wN (η) = (1 − η2 )−1/2 . The Cauchy data are not further normalized to have unit boundary norm. 3. If the eigenbasis is real-valued, there is a density-one set Snod such that the number of nodal domains of uj, the connected components of Q \ {uj = 0}, tends to infinity as λj → ∞ with j ∈ Snod.
